items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.raw_text: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions. OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it. items.title: datasette-llm 0.1a9
items.raw_text: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a9 I have some big upgrades to Datasette Agent in the pipeline, but in the meantime here's a tiny user experience improvement to the underlying datasette-llm plugin. It now picks up the default model used by LLM , which means you can start using Datasette Agent without needing to explicitly configure a default model: uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db Previously you would also need to specify a model with -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model gpt-6-astra . items.title: MetLib 2026 | Day 4: Resilience, Solidarity and Letters to the Future
items.raw_text: The final day of MetLib 2026 was perhaps the most emotional, bringing the conference’s discussions about resilience, community and the future of libraries into a deeply human perspective. In a moving opening keynote, Yuliya Vaganova, Director of the Khanenko Museum in Kyiv, Ukraine , shared the experience of keeping a cultural institution alive during wartime. Despite the destruction caused by the war, the museum continued to find ways to connect with its community through innovative programmes, some of which received European recognition. Among the most powerful examples were performances by a theatre group featuring actors with Down syndrome and a blood donation campaign — a reminder of how essential solidarity becomes in times of crisis. Looking towards the future, participants also took part in scenario-planning workshops , exploring possible futures and reflecting on how libraries might prepare for the challenges and opportunities ahead. One of the most personal moments of the conference was an invitation to write letters to the future . Throughout the event, participants had received messages written from the perspective of a fellow librarian living in the future. On the final day, they responded with handwritten letters of their own, sharing personal reflections, hopes and questions inspired by the conference. The organisers plan to publish these letters one by one in the coming months, extending the conversation beyond MetLib 2026. The conference concluded in Rotterda

items.title: New infographic highlights key recommendations for inclusive library services
items.raw_text: The IFLA Libraries Serving Persons with Print Disabilities (LPD) Section has published an infographic providing a visual overview of the key themes and recommendations in the Guidelines for Inclusive Library Services for Persons with Print Disabilities . The infographic highlights practical areas such as inclusive library spaces, accessible formats and reading tools, accessibility metadata, communication, cooperation and programming. It illustrates how libraries can respond to different users’ needs and make their services more accessible and inclusive. The Guidelines are designed to support libraries and library staff in developing, maintaining and improving accessible and inclusive services for persons with print disabilities. Explore the infographic and the full Guidelines in the IFLA Repository.

Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
items.raw_text: Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it's the middle of the night while the clock says it's lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans. A new Science study on Manx shearwaters, seabirds that can fly hundreds of kilometers a day over the North Atlantic, shows they jet-lag themselves during their excursions. And because these birds navigate by the Sun, that jet lag leaves a measurable mark—it skews their compass. Clockwork compass Patrick Lewin is a behavioral and sensory ecologist at the University of Oxford and lead author of the study. “Manx shearwaters are medium-sized birds, about the same size as a pigeon,” Lewin said. “They are white underneath and black on top, but they have very long wings, and they are closely related to albatross.” Manx shearwaters nest in burrows on coastal islands around the North Atlantic. Most breed around the UK and Ireland, with about half of their population living in Wales. Read full article Comments

items.title: The FDA wants to pull its approval of a drug. It’s not so easy.
items.raw_text: In May 2021, the US Food and Drug Administration released a lengthy briefing document on an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis that often damages the kidneys and lungs. The agency was on the fence about whether to approve the treatment, and it wanted an independent advisory committee to weigh in. Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies? Participants in the study, which had been conducted by the California biotechnology company ChemoCentryx, did appear to have slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year. But according to the FDA, it was hard to interpret the results because the study’s design had been less than optimal. Some advisory committee members expressed a similar view. The effect of the drug, said one, “is just not well verified by this study.” At the same time, many patients, and some physicians, saw in the data a potentially helpful medication, one that might lessen patients’ reliance on steroids, which are highly effective but often cause severe side effects. The company also said in a post on X that, while withdrawals remain paused, they're on track to be enabled on Sunday. items.title: Best Buy is bundling a $100 gift card with touchscreen MacBook Pro preorders
items.raw_text: We got a chance to touch Apple’s latest MacBook at the “Pro and Tell” event. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge While the new touch-enabled MacBook Pro with the PROLED XDR screen is available for preorder across a few major retailers, Best Buy is sweetening the deal by including a $100 gift card. The gift card will be automatically added to your cart when you preorder one of Apple’s highest-end laptops available in 14- or 16-inch configurations, and even one of its 14-inch MacBook Pro laptops with the M6 chip. You can verify that it’s been added to your order in the “Complete your purchase” section of the checkout page. Apple MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display Where to Buy: $2899 at Best Buy (w/ $100 gift card) My colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto got a chance to check out the new laptop at Apple’s event, and came away impressed by the Tandem OLED panel’s brightness and contrast, but described the update as “kind of boring” given the relatively small changes to the system otherwise. There are some unique changes to macOS that help make the new touch experience smoother, like magnifying the traffic light-colored buttons on windows when you move your finger near them. The PROLED laptops are also a bit thinner and lighter than standard models, and the Apple logo on the back glows like on older versions. Read our MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display hands-on .
